ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: At the top, an L-shaped domino made of 4 small squares is given; the shape is 3 squares connected in a row, with 1 more square attached at the end. Below there are 4 candidate figures, and each candidate figure is made of 8 small squares. Then reason: what the question asks is whether each candidate figure can be divided into two identical L-shaped dominoes, with rotation allowed. Look at them one by one: (1) The 1st is a 2×4 rectangle, which can be divided into two Ls: one uses the 3 squares standing vertically on the left plus the upper-right-corner 1 square, and the other uses the 3 squares standing vertically on the right plus the lower-left-corner 1 square. (2) The 2nd figure can also be divided into two Ls: the top and the right side form one L, and the remaining lower-left part forms another L. (3) The 3rd figure can be divided into an L of “3 connected squares at the top plus the lower-left-corner 1 square,” and the remaining part is another L piece. (4) The 4th figure can be divided into the vertical L on the left side and the horizontal L at the bottom. Therefore all 4 candidate figures can be made with two L-shaped pieces.

method.method_draft: First read the image: the given L-tile is a 4-square tetromino made from a row of 3 squares with one extra square attached at an end. Then inspect each of the four lower candidate shapes and try to partition its 8 unit squares into two copies of this L, allowing rotations/turns. Work left to right: (1) the 2-by-4 rectangle can be split into one L using the top three cells of the left column plus the top-right cell, and a second L using the bottom three cells of the right column plus the bottom-left cell. (2) the second shape can be split into the top/middle right-column L and the lower left-column L. (3) the third shape can be split into the top row plus one square below the left end, and the remaining vertical strip plus bottom-right square. (4) the fourth shape can be split into the tall left-side L and the bottom-row/right-side L. Since all four candidates admit such a two-L tiling, count all 4 shapes.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the top displayed L tetromino as the required 4-square piece, and read the four lower 8-square target shapes from left to right, including their grid-cell arrangements.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to know there are exactly two L shapes, together covering 8 squares, and that the task is to count how many of the 4 displayed shapes can be made.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the exact-cover rule for polyomino tiling: a target shape is possible if its 8 unit squares can be covered by two non-overlapping congruent L tetrominoes, with rotations allowed.
